source.title: Irish News, 1 May 1933, p. 3 ("Magherafelt Rural nominations")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Irish News 1 May 1933 p3 'Magherafelt Rural Nominations', read in the block images (INW19330501.2.43, areas 15-30, reassembled by their page positions): 'The following twenty-five members were returned unopposed' (names and labels, without divisions); 'Two candidates were nominated for Tobermore Division'; 'Three of the members returned are new - Mrs. Higgins ... for Magherafelt Division; David W. Wallace ... and David M'Clure ...'. 'Of the members returned twelve are Nationalist and 13 Unionist.'

note: Triennial rural district council election. Polling in the Tobermore division took place on Friday 2 June 1933 and the votes were counted at Magherafelt on Saturday 3 June. No other division was contested: twenty-five members were returned unopposed at the nominations on Friday 28 April 1933 (Irish News, 1 May 1933, p. 3). Filed on 1933-06-02, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Londonderry that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1933-06-01 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Twenty-three unopposed returns added from the Irish News list (meetings gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). New member: 'Mrs. Higgins, widow of the late Sir Lawrence Higgins, for Magherafelt Division'. Returned unopposed.
